surfaces.label: Device HTTP responses can stall discovery indefinitely
surfaces.notes: `search()` synchronously forwards network-selected LOCATION to `post()`. Blocking connect/write/header/body reads have no absolute deadline; the UDP `select` timeout is suspended while `post()` runs.

surfaces.label: Device HTTP responses can exhaust caller memory
surfaces.notes: `post()` reads complete lines, appends headers and EOF/chunked bodies, and passes peer-selected Content-Length/chunk sizes directly to `read()`. There is no maximum line/header/chunk/body budget before buffering.

surfaces.label: SSDP responses can trigger blind requests to loopback services
surfaces.notes: `recv()` discards sender provenance; URL-pattern matching is the only destination gate. Parsed host/port/path reach `inet_aton()` and `connect()` without a resolved-address or peer-origin policy. Service endpoint construction likewise accepts absolute cross-origin URLs.

surfaces.label: Repeated SSDP packets keep discovery running and growing
surfaces.notes: The full timeout is recomputed for each `select()` iteration rather than measured against a fixed end time. Packet count, fetch count and result count are unbounded, and responses are not deduplicated before fetching/appending.
surfaces.riskArea: Missing discovery duration and result budgets

surfaces.label: Gateway success responses cause endless mapping enumeration
surfaces.notes: The unconditional loop stops only on peer-supplied non-200 status, increments the index and pushes every response without an entry or elapsed-time cap.

surfaces.label: Cyclic media containers cause unbounded recursive traversal
surfaces.notes: Remote DIDL container IDs are copied into objects and passed back as ObjectID by every recursive call. None of the three example walkers tracks already-visited containers; dms2vodcast requested_count limits conversions only.
surfaces.riskArea: Unbounded traversal of remote object graph

surfaces.label: Media metadata can alter generated RSS XML structure
surfaces.notes: SOAP entity-decoded DIDL is regex-extracted rather than validated; its title enters the item info hash unchanged, then a heredoc emits it as XML. Filename substitutions remove slashes/spaces but leave XML-significant quotes and angle brackets.
surfaces.riskArea: Missing XML text and attribute escaping

surfaces.label: Converter Shell execution boundary
surfaces.notes: examples/dms2vodcast.pl:6,272-306 imports external Shell and passes remote URL/names in complete option strings. No dependency implementation/version is available offline. Original candidate retained in deferred; no confirmed RCE claim.

surfaces.label: XML parsing and generic SOAP caller authority
surfaces.notes: Device.pm:90-102, ActionResponse.pm:105-120 and HTTP.pm:188-202 use regex/literal replacements, with no entity resolver; no XXE path. Service.pm:217-245,303-319 lacks XML escaping, but generic caller APIs do not establish a distinct restricted-user authority boundary. Remote service controls itself; no additional privilege crossing established.

surfaces.label: Unix converter filename traversal
surfaces.notes: examples/dms2vodcast.pl:285-287 replaces every slash, defeating ordinary ../ in remote names. Windows separator behavior and local symlink attacks are not established; no arbitrary file-write claim.
